post.description:
Accepts a question and returns 202 at once with a `run_id` and `status: queued`. The research (searches, page reads, reflection, a cited answer) runs in the background.

Flow: 1) POST here. 2) Poll `GET /agent/research/{run_id}` until `status` is `done` (read `result`) or `failed` (read `error`). `result` holds the answer, the retrieval date, the `claims` with their sources and whether each rests on a full page (`fetched`) or a snippet, the cited `sources`, the `also_found` links, and the `unsupported` counts (statements removed, by reason).

A 409 means the same request is already running. The run id is random and only its owner can read it; anyone else gets the same 404 as for an unknown id. `POST /agent/ask` is the earlier synchronous endpoint and is unchanged.

get.description: `run_id` is the random token returned by `POST /agent/research`. Only the user who started the run can read it: for anyone else, and for an unknown id, the answer is the same 404.
get.summary: Status and result of a research run

post.description:
Accepts the job and returns 202 at once with a `run_id` and `status: queued`. The preparation (job analysis, research, CV tailoring, email draft, grounding check) runs in the background and ends at `awaiting_review`, with the application stored as `prepared`.

Flow: 1) POST here. 2) Poll `GET /applications/preparations/{run_id}` every few seconds until `status` is `awaiting_review` (read `application_id`, then `GET /applications/{application_id}`), `closed`, or `failed` (read `error`). 3) Review, then approve and send through their own endpoints. Preparing never approves or sends. A 409 means a run for the same recipient and job title is already active.

get.summary: How mail is sent by this server: dry_run, redirected or real

schema.title: Response Put Master Cv Applications Master Cv Put

get.description:
`run_id` is the random token returned by `POST /applications`, not a sequential number. Only the user who started the run can read it: for anyone else the answer is 404, the same as for a run that does not exist.

`status`: `queued`, `running`, `awaiting_review` (the application is ready to review), `closed` (the workflow record is finished), or `failed` (see `error`). `step` names the graph node in progress. `stalled` is true when the run has sent no heartbeat for `PREPARATION_STALE_SECONDS`. Stalled runs are recovered at startup.

Poll every few seconds. Stop when the status is `awaiting_review`, `closed` or `failed`.
